threats.title: SQL injection enables authentication bypass in login query
threats.description: The login query is constructed by string concatenation with user-supplied email and password, allowing SQL injection attacks to bypass authentication. An attacker can inject SQL syntax (e.g., ' OR 1=1--) to authenticate as any user without knowing their password.
threats.attack_scenario: An attacker sends a POST request to /rest/user/login with email set to "admin@juice-sh.op' --" and any password. The injected SQL comment bypasses the password check, and the attacker is authenticated as the admin user.

evidence.snippet: models.sequelize.query(`SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' AND password = '${security.hash(req.body.password || '')}' AND deletedAt IS NULL`, { model: UserModel, plain: true })

threats.recommendation: Use parameterized queries instead of string concatenation. Replace the raw SQL query with Sequelize's built-in findOne method: await UserModel.findOne({ where: { email: req.body.email, password: security.hash(req.body.password), deletedAt: null } })

threats.title: Credential stuffing attack via unthrottled login endpoint
threats.description: The /rest/user/login endpoint has no rate limiting, throttling, lockout mechanism, or CAPTCHA protection. An attacker can perform unlimited login attempts using a corpus of breached credentials, enabling credential stuffing attacks to compromise user accounts.
threats.attack_scenario: An attacker uses a tool to send thousands of login requests per second with email/password pairs from a known breach. Without rate limiting, the attacker can test thousands of credentials in minutes and identify valid accounts.

evidence.snippet: app.use('/rest/user/reset-password', rateLimit({ windowMs: 5 * 60 * 1000, max: 100, keyGenerator ({ headers, ip }: { headers: any, ip: any }) { return headers['X-Forwarded-For'] ?? ip } }))

threats.recommendation: Apply rate limiting middleware to the login endpoint. Example: app.post('/rest/user/login', rateLimit({ windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000, max: 5, keyGenerator: ({ headers, ip }) => headers['X-Forwarded-For'] ?? ip }), login()). Consider also implementing account lockout after N failed attempts and CAPTCHA challenges.
